title: Annual Property Charges on File: Review Cycle, Evidence and Figures
content:
Every set-aside under Set-Aside Accounts that pays or funds property charges holds an annual property tax, an annual hazard premium and an annual flood premium on file.

## Clauses

1. The annual property charges on file are reviewed at the plan's review interval in months and whenever a new bill is received, and are updated only from the evidence the plan names.
2. The annual charges on file are updated only from a property tax, hazard insurance or flood insurance bill on file for that set-aside.
3. The annual property tax is the sum of the billed amounts of every installment bill of the current tax year; the annual hazard premium is the billed amount of the current hazard policy term; and the annual flood premium is the billed amount of the current flood policy term.
4. An update never changes a Partially Funded LESA's fixed semi-annual installment and never adds funds to the set-aside.
5. When the updated charges leave the balance projected to cover fewer than the plan's low-balance notice months of the charges the set-aside pays, the borrower receives a low-balance notice.

## Retired parts of clause 3

Each of the three figures in clause 3 is **no longer in force** for a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve, and only for such a reserve, where the reserve's figure is the projected figure held under the current basis:

- "The annual property tax is the sum of the billed amounts of every installment bill of the current tax year" — no longer in force for a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve; the annual property tax of every other set-aside remains under clause 3.
- "the annual hazard premium is the billed amount of the current hazard policy term" — no longer in force for a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve; the annual hazard premium of every other set-aside remains under clause 3.
- "the annual flood premium is the billed amount of the current flood policy term" — no longer in force for a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve; the annual flood premium of every other set-aside remains under clause 3.

## Hypothetical example (a Fully Funded LESA)

A LESA's file shows two installment bills of the current tax year, 1,350.00 and 1,350.00, a current hazard term billed at 1,180.00 and a current flood term billed at 640.00. The annual property tax on file becomes 2,700.00, the hazard premium 1,180.00 and the flood premium 640.00; the balance and any fixed installment are unchanged by the update.

the annual hazard premium is the billed_amount of the current hazard policy term
the annual flood premium is the billed_amount of the current flood policy term
